finding: Global multi-repository accessibility audit established a major open-data gap in human biomechanics: no public dataset exists combining synchronized dynamometer active torque, joint angle, angular velocity, MVC normalization, and simultaneous surface EMG from both agonists (VL/RF/VM) and antagonists (BF/ST) across independent individuals.

Biomechanical sensitivity analysis established that patellar tendon regional morphometry creates a ~22% stress concentration at the narrower proximal insertion (38.46 MPa vs 31.50 MPa at 4 kN). Under a hypothetical +20% muscle force gain (4.8 kN), proximal stress rises to 46.15 MPa, causing an estimated 60-75% reduction in cyclic fatigue life under the Wöhler power law, demonstrating that tendon fatigue life—not single-cycle yield—is the primary mechanical safety bottleneck.

Systematic audit of MTJCore replication history clarified that the myonuclear program has NOT achieved three independent replications: Stage 5 had high within-study concordance (92.09%) but was dominated by a single donor (51.2% of myonuclei); Stage 6 failed its pre-registered replication threshold (0.5818 vs 0.60); and Stage 7 showed only 23.1% directional agreement between RNA and protein, confirming an extensive translational gap between transcript abundance and structural extracellular matrix.

title: Anthropometric-Kinematic Dominance and Antagonist sEMG Noise in Cross-Subject Knee Torque Prediction
statement: In Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation across 20 healthy adults (125 extension trials), raw uncalibrated surface antagonist EMG does not improve torque prediction over agonist-only models (RMSE 89.10 Nm vs 82.85 Nm, paired p = 0.1426). Incorporating joint angle and anthropometrics (mass, height, biological sex) reduces RMSE by 41% to 53.45 Nm and explains 63.0% of torque variance.

title: In Vivo Intra-Tendinous Sliding and Layer-Dependent Displacement Gradient in Human Achilles Tendon
statement: Ultrasound speckle tracking across 10 healthy adults (160 observations) demonstrates statistically significant displacement non-uniformity across depth layers (Friedman p = 1.17e-13). During isometric plantarflexion, the deep tendon layer displaces 23.1% more than the superficial layer (3.00 mm vs 2.44 mm), with inter-layer sliding differences of 0.28 to 0.40 mm.

title: Stromal Microanatomical Specialization at the Human Myotendinous Junction in the Oxford Single-Cell Atlas
statement: Cohen et al. (2026) single-cell atlas independently confirms that stromal fibroblasts residing at the human MTJ are transcriptionally distinct and upregulate COL22A1, POSTN, TNC, and COMP, validating stromal participation in the myotendinous attachment matrix.

title: Anthropometric-Kinematic Dominance and Antagonist sEMG Noise in Cross-Subject Knee Torque Prediction
statement: In a 2x5 factorial ablation on 125 extension trials (DPValid), anthropometry and angle alone (F0) achieve R2 = 0.6867 (RMSE = 49.19 Nm). Adding surface EMG degrades performance, and adding antagonist EMG to anthropometry + agonist EMG statistically significantly increases error (Delta RMSE = -3.01 Nm, paired t p = 0.0089).

title: Subject-Level Invariant of Deep-over-Superficial Achilles Tendon Displacement with Non-Significant Strain Gradient
statement: Proper subject-level re-analysis (N=10) of Bogaerts et al. resolves pseudoreplication (correcting chi2 from 59.55 to 20.0, p = 4.54e-05) and confirms that deep displacement exceeds superficial displacement in 100% of participants (+0.564 mm, p = 0.0031). However, layer strain differences are statistically non-significant (p = 0.6703).

title: Stromal-Myonuclear Dual Synthesis of Type XXII Collagen at Human MTJ Interface
statement: Cohen et al. (2026) single-cell atlas demonstrates that tendon-resident MTJ fibroblasts specialize transcriptionally and express COL22A1, POSTN, TNC, and COMP, establishing that the junctional attachment matrix is a co-product of both muscle myonuclei and specialized tendon fibroblasts.

title: Oxford Achilles Atlas Provenance Identity with MTJCore Discovery Cohort
statement: The Oxford Achilles Tendon Atlas (Cohen et al. 2026, CZ CELLxGENE ef0fc6ac-4872-40e1-ab24-e445b19ca6e3) is the original discovery dataset of the MTJCore project, containing 64,862 cells (22,146 muscle nuclei, 24,179 fibroblasts) across 5 human donors. Evaluating MTJCore on this dataset constitutes complete training-data leakage (circular self-validation) and cannot serve as an independent replication.

title: Correction of Cycle 17 Methodological Errors and Erroneous GEO Accession
statement: Forensic audit rectified four critical issues from Cycle 17: (1) HYP-0008 verified status preserved under its original biophysical scope, as EXP-0054 confirms uncalibrated sEMG unidentifiability; (2) HYP-0010 restored to patellar tendon segmental CSA; (3) Ridge F3 vs F0 t-statistic typo corrected to t = -0.084, p = 0.9337; (4) accession GSE130649 (mouse inner ear organoids) falsified and permanently eliminated from human muscle plans.

title: Human Quadriceps Specific Tension Identification and Sex-Invariance
statement: Analysis of N=20 adults (100 maximal isometric extension trials, DPValid) yields in vivo quadriceps specific tension sigma = 27.22 +/- 4.84 N/cm2 (95% CI [25.09, 29.34]), strictly invariant between sexes (males 27.08 +/- 5.16 vs females 27.37 +/- 4.79 N/cm2, Welch t = -0.134, p = 0.8946). A 1-parameter physics PCSA model achieves R2 = 0.6758 out-of-sample under LOSO CV, matching multi-parameter regression M1 (R2 = 0.6820), whereas uncalibrated sEMG degrades prediction to R2 = 0.6301.

title: Tendon Fatigue Wöhler Calibration and Hypertrophic Compensation Threshold
statement: Empirical calibration of human tendon S-N fatigue response yields Wöhler slope B = 8.45. Under unadapted +20% muscle force (S1), tendon cyclic fatigue life is reduced by -86.7% (retention 0.133x baseline) despite preserving static safety factor SF = 2.06. Restoring baseline fatigue life requires compensatory tendon remodeling of Delta CSA >= 15% (or Delta UTS >= 10%), demonstrating that fatigue durability, not static tensile yield, is the primary mechanical constraint on human strength enhancement.

title: The Isomass Power Penalty: Analytical and Empirical Proof of Power Loss under Fixed Muscle Volume Pennation Remodeling
statement: Under an isomass constraint (V = const), increasing muscle pennation angle from 14 deg to 18 deg increases isometric torque by +25.20% (from 306.8 to 384.1 Nm), but causes an unavoidable geometric fascicle shortening from 8.40 to 6.58 cm (-21.71%). While normalized shortening speed remains constant (10.0 s^-1), absolute contraction velocity drops by -21.71% (0.840 to 0.658 m/s). By Hill's mechanical power relation, peak dynamic power is strictly scaled by cos(theta)/cos(theta0), producing a net -1.98% drop in peak power. Pennation alone cannot enhance dynamic explosive capability.

title: The Tendon Iso-Durability Conservation Invariant: (1 + Delta_CSA) * (1 + Delta_UTS) >= lambda_F
statement: Mathematical and empirical analysis of human tendon S-N fatigue mechanics established the exact conservation law governing fatigue life preservation under augmented muscle force: (1 + Delta_CSA) * (1 + Delta_UTS) >= lambda_F. For a +20% force augmentation (lambda_F = 1.20), unadapted loading causes an 86.67% fatigue life collapse (0.133x retention, stress 46.15 MPa). A combined biological adaptation of Delta_CSA >= 15% and Delta_UTS >= 10% (Case 2C, actual stress 40.13 MPa, stress ratio 0.3841) fully restores and exceeds baseline durability (1.678x retention), providing a proven mechanical safety envelope.

title: 3-DOF Closed-Chain Leg Press Equilibrium Bounds and DPValid Paired Subject-Cluster Bootstrap
statement: Linear-programming closure of sagittal 3-DOF lower-limb static equilibrium (hip-knee Jacobian block plus flat-foot COP and friction constraints without pseudoinverse shortcuts) shows that coordinated chain-wide Strategy 2 increases modeled bilateral leg-press force by +21.64% at 100 deg internal knee angle (eta_chain = 0.988), whereas isolated +20% quadriceps enhancement transfers only +15.27% (eta_chain = 0.764). On single-joint DPValid reference (N=20, 125 trials), paired subject-cluster bootstrap (B=10,000) of pooled out-of-sample R2 yields +0.0735 (95% CI [+0.0259, +0.1428]) for M2 PCSA vs Baseline F0 and +0.0081 ([-0.0903, +0.1173]) vs age-adjusted M1.

title: Deep-Layer Enthesis Stress Concentration Under Ballistic dF/dt and Tendon-Paced Remodeling Recovery
statement: Integrating Bogaerts et al. (2017, N=10) in vivo layer displacement partitioning (deep/superficial ratio = 1.2315, k_deep = 1.1204) with Kongsgaard (2007) proximal patellar CSA (104.0 mm2) and Standard Linear Solid viscoelasticity shows that at dF/dt = 20,000 N/s, local deep-enthesis von Mises stress at 4800 N (+20% EXP-0060 baseline) rises from nominal 46.15 MPa to 58.83 MPa (SF_local = 1.61) unadapted, restored to 50.99 MPa (SF_local = 2.05) under Case 2C (+15% CSA, +10% UTS). Synchronization of muscle progression strictly inside the FND-0063 tendon capacity curve (regime H2) eliminates the transient remodeling damage spike (1.00x vs 2.94x under uncoordinated H1).

title: Energy-Conserving 4-Layer Pennes Bioheat Intermittent Feasibility Envelope for 2700 s
statement: Using a backward-Euler 4-shell cylindrical Pennes bioheat + central arterial pool solver (First-Law closure error 0.00 J) anchored to Malaga CPET (N=846) and ACTES metabolic rates, intermittent duty-cycle pacing keeps modeled core temperature below 39.5 C over 2700 s at 360 W +20% effort up to D_max = 0.92 in temperate climate (20 C, 50% RH), 0.74 in warm (28 C, 60% RH), 0.65 in hot-humid (32 C, 80% RH), and 0.59 in hot-dry (35 C, 30% RH), while maintaining strict compatibility with tools/cpe45.py (target_achievement = not_assessed).

title: Unified Architecture A Canonical Specification and Master Roadmap Adjudication
statement: Synthesis of EXP-0059 through EXP-0063 into the canonical Architecture A specification confirms theoretical conditional feasibility of ~20% whole-limb strength augmentation only under co-adapted hip/knee/ankle musculature, coordinated tendon CSA (+15%) and UTS (+10%) pacing, and intermittent thermal duty budgeting or 100-500 W continuous vascular heat removal, while preserving TARGET-CPE45 = NOT EXTERNALLY VALIDATED, BIOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS = NO_GO, and EXP-0061 bilateral leg press = DATA_BLOCKED.

title: Byte-exact archive replay and work mismatch in original thermal contrast
statement: EXP-0061–0064 replayed byte-for-byte. The archived intermittent 360 W-peak schedules deliver 619–903 kJ over 2700 s, versus 972 kJ at constant 360 W. Fixed model calculations only.

title: Limited external thermal transfer on hot cycling cohort
statement: Among 23 eligible participants model MAE for 1-to-45-minute rectal temperature change was 0.586 C versus 1.275 C persistence and 1.048 C lumped baseline. Paired bootstrap baseline-minus-model CI [0.501, 0.865] C. Fixed nominal initial tissue state and 5–6-minute environment limit application; CPE45 not assessed.

title: Conditional one-factor robustness of static leg-press gain
statement: The rounded coordinated-chain gain stayed above 20% in tested one-factor grids: 21.31–21.83% at 100 degrees and 20.86–21.63% at 140 degrees for common specific-tension multiplier 0.7–1.3. Tendon constraints and joint uncertainty are not tested.

title: Conditional tendon gate depends on leg press posture
statement: Under moment-to-force proxy and the specified CSA/UTS/rate grid, coordinated-chain 100-degree case yields local SF 1.035–1.376; 140-degree case SF 1.406–1.890. These model-only outcomes do not establish tissue safety or whole-system performance.

title: Controlled 1.25-fold adaptation-rate scenario
statement: With identical tendon trajectory and load, changing muscle time constant from 16 to 12.8 days changes peak model daily damage ratio from 2.30 to 2.56; this is not measured human injury risk or demonstration of TARGET-ADAPT25.

title: Initial gradient dominates early thermal drift in Fujii exploratory comparison
statement: In 24 pre-exercise sessions of six participants, mean observed esophageal change was +0.020 C over 270 s; nominal-layer solver predicted -0.485 C at zero external power, whereas uniform 37 C initialization predicted -0.018 C. Neither input configuration is an independently calibrated initial state.

title: Uniform initial temperature worsens fit on previously viewed hot cycling dataset
statement: On 23 previously evaluated participants, uniform 37 C initial state gave MAE 0.719 C versus 0.586 C for nominal initial state, paired nominal-minus-uniform error CI [-0.206,-0.061] C; this is exploratory reuse and does not validate initial tissue temperatures.

title: Variation in actual power and climate on McLaughlin cohort
statement: Under post hoc interpretation of numeric timestamps as interval ends, 23 complete power profiles yield integrated work 0–16.24% below first-minute constant power, median -2.73%; within-person humidity range 3–14 percentage points. Temperature prediction effect remains untested.

title: Recorded workload changes thermal prediction error
statement: On 23 previously assessed McLaughlin participants, nominal constant-input thermal MAE 0.586 C changed to 0.475 C using recorded minute power; paired constant-minus-variable error CI [0.022,0.222] C. Numeric time-label interpretation and initial temperatures remain assumptions.

title: Conditional chain-tendon and thermal interface exposes missing endpoints
statement: At common prescribed 621 kJ work, 75 kg and 20 C, the static 100-degree enhanced chain has conditional tendon SF 1.285 and 140-degree case 1.747; thermal model peak core 37.975 C is identical across cases. Dynamic fatigue, motor control and post45 remain not assessed.

title: Conditional tendon gate sensitive to assumed moment arm
statement: At CSA multiplier 1.15, UTS 1.08 and 20 kN/s, the arm multiplier needed for local SF 1.5 is 1.175 at 100 degrees and 0.853 at 140 degrees, holding LP torque fixed. Diagnostic interface sensitivity only.

title: Static reoptimization changes interpretation of arm sensitivity
statement: When quadriceps moment arm is scaled consistently in LP and tendon conversion, arm multipliers 0.8–1.2 yield SF approximately 1.285 at 100 degrees and 1.747 at 140 degrees for the specified CSA, UTS and force-rate assumptions; model-only, no safety validation.

title: Retrospective velocity-loss relationship with held participants
statement: For 23 postmenopausal women, participant-held-out linear description of velocity loss by retrospectively known completed-set percentage had participant-weighted MAE 9.16 versus 11.86 percentage points for a constant; paired gain CI [1.60, 3.80]. Final velocity loss ranged 11.9–59.8%. Not an online predictor or architecture validation.

title: Squat moment scale is sensitive to platform moment interpretation
statement: For AB01 and AB02 the ratio of reconstructed/source knee moment slope to mass changes from 1.089 and 0.574 using all plate-moment components to 0.990 and 0.952 when horizontal components are zeroed, with correlations 0.99987 and 0.99994. This conditional finding does not establish which platform moment convention is correct; ISS-0028 remains open.

title: Conditional moment-scale relationship transfers within the same cohort
statement: In two held participants, vertical-only platform moment reconstruction yields slope/mass 0.734 and 0.893 on unloaded squats (both within preregistered broad 0.7–1.3); correlations are 0.99971 and 0.99993. AB03 still differs by 26.6% from unity. Convention and physical accuracy remain unresolved.

title: Conditional energy ledger can drive the thermal interface at common work
statement: For the conditional 2700 s 60/40 protocol, D2 yields 403–432 kJ against 583.2 kJ demanded across three assumed fatigue rates; coupling transfers D2 heat to the thermal solver with energy closure. This is model-only, D2 transfer previously failed, and no whole-architecture effect is established.

title: Exploratory 60-minute thermal transfer with recorded workload
statement: On 23 previously viewed McLaughlin participants, 60–1 minute temperature-change MAE is 0.733 C for variable-power Pennes vs 1.376 C for persistence and 1.078 C for participant-mass lumped balance; Pennes superiority CI relative to persistence [0.227, 0.972] C. Rectal versus mean-body endpoints and timestamp assumptions limit interpretation.

title: Open bilateral leg press cohort provides scoped force trajectory
statement: Eleven participants had W0 mean peak force 2513.6 N and mean paired W0-to-POS change 19.37% [9.26,31.69] bootstrap CI; five participants increased at least 20%. No parallel control, individual mass or geometry, and no inference of target or architecture efficacy.

title: Closed-chain hip posture input is unused
statement: EXP-0061 posture_kinematics has zero reads of theta_hip_flex_deg; changing both posture inputs to 40, 78 or 110 degrees leaves all saved LP scenario outputs unchanged. This is a model implementation limitation, not a physiological invariance.

title: Finite differences expose double-counted gravity term
statement: For the potential energy specified in EXP-0061, the original hip gravity term adds the shank-foot derivative twice. At internal knee 100 degrees finite difference is -33.072 Nm, original -42.110 Nm, corrected -33.072 Nm. Correction is an arithmetic result within the existing model, not physiological validation.

title: Gravity-corrected chain and dependent scenarios rebuilt
statement: The isolated one-line gravity correction recomputes all 48 tendon cases, 23 one-factor cases, 24 interface cases, 10 arm reoptimizations, integrated fixed-work and D2 thermal scenarios, and the legacy numerical aggregator. Strategy 2 gains are 21.93% at 100 degrees and 21.77% at 140 degrees; no tendon proxy gate changed in the tested grid. Model-only and not whole-system validation.

title: Chord direction sensitivity in corrected static chain
statement: Across five fixed diagnostic chord angles, modeled strategy 2 gains range 21.86–22.04%, 21.83–21.98%, and 21.73–21.84% for knee angles 100, 110 and 140 degrees. Conditional tendon proxy passes the joint model gate only at 140 degrees. This is not a measurement of human function, tissue safety or hip posture.

title: Force sensitivity to friction with conditional gate retained
statement: At knee 140 degrees model strategy force spans 4041.9 to 4632.6 N across mu 0 to 0.8 while modeled relative gain spans 21.58–21.96%; conditional force and tissue gate holds on the tested grid only at 140 degrees, not 100 or 110. No human safety or functional conclusion follows.

title: Differential fatigue assumption can change modeled force gate
statement: With shared D2 trace at fatigue rate 0.003/s and alpha=1.05, minimum modeled force gain is 19.57% at 100 degrees and 19.40% at 140 degrees; alpha=1 retains static gain algebraically. Alpha and the force mapping are unmeasured counterfactuals, not physiological predictions.

title: Four directional outcomes can be jointly traced but post mass is unavailable
statement: The four prespecified directional changes occur in 12/24 experimental and 3/24 control records; mean direction alone does not establish meaningful effects. All paired mass values are identical because the source dictionary labels mass baseline-only; matched post mass cannot be inferred.

title: Recovery dataset requires identity and mechanical-scale clarification
statement: Four workbooks contain 48 supplied Subject_ID strings, none linked to both conditions within its workbook; 362/384 pre repetition entries are noninteger and 960/960 TW values exceed diagnostic 3 m/s with reported units m/s. Different IDs, averages or scale transformations may explain these findings; no data integrity conclusion is drawn.

title: Individual plantar torque trajectory after fatiguing protocol
statement: In 12 selected men mean post, 5-minute and 10-minute MVC torque ratios to baseline are 0.744, 0.909 and 0.936, respectively. Measurements follow the published protocol including electrical stimulation and vibration; no causal or whole-system inference.

title: Published MVC means agree with alternative trial aggregation
statement: Article-specified best-of-three yields 714.10/666.51/682.54 N for condition MT1 versus published 662/596/625 N; post-hoc mean-of-three yields 662.39/595.80/625.11 N. Trial mapping and processing are unconfirmed; this does not prove an error in the source.

title: Force threshold detectability depends strongly on uncertainty and effect margin
statement: Under an illustrative two-group noncentral t model with SD of individual change 29.7/1.96 percentage points, the minimal n per group for 80% power to show a contrast >20 percentage points is 711 at true 22 and 115 at true 25. This is not an actual trial sample size or efficacy estimate.

title: Persistence is a necessary baseline for this group torque trajectory
statement: On previously viewed published group means, persistence from 4 minutes gives 2.88 Nm equal-condition MAE at 6–12 minutes versus 4.43 Nm for a 2-to-4-minute line extrapolation. At VHI predictions coincide due to rounding. No statistical or individual validation follows.

title: Zero-fatigue D2 matches persistence for conditional constant-demand scenario
statement: On 23 previously viewed participants, D2 with zero fatigue and observed first-minute demand proxy exactly matches the persistence prediction over the later 44 min, both MAE 6.92 W. This equality is model- and task-specific, not evidence of physiological validity.

title: Separating demand and hypothetical capacity reduces constant-load scenario error
statement: For 23 previously viewed participants, D2-cap power MAE is 8.07 W versus original 33.45 W under first-minute demand and P1/0.6 capacity assumptions; persistence MAE is 6.92 W. This does not establish independent validation or a physiologically measured capacity.

title: First-sprint scaling reduces absolute D2 error but leaves substantial relative-shape error
statement: At rate 0.003/s, first-sprint normalization reduces tenth-sprint MAE from 742.52 to 345.61 W in Chmura and 339.56 to 302.32 W in Jutlah; relative ratio errors are 30.76 and 55.28 percentage points. This is an empirical bridge, not an energy-balanced power trajectory or physiological validation.

title: New passive-control sprint cohort has uncertain model versus persistence advantage
statement: In 12 previously unused participants, normalized D2 predicts fifth-sprint mean power with assumed-unit MAE 84.75 versus persistence 88.09; paired difference 3.35 [−30.31,36.27]. Unit W is inferred and the source was partly previewed; no efficacy or whole-system inference.

title: Observed paired endurance times differ where D2 condition input is absent
statement: In 18 previously unused participants, observed Stroop minus control time averages −111.06 s with paired bootstrap [−190.73,−48.94]; the D2 model produces exactly zero contrast because its inputs are identical across conditions. The endpoint definition differs and no physiological mechanism is identified.

title: D2 95% threshold is crossed after internal demand reduction
statement: In both nonzero-rate scenarios, all 18 first threshold windows begin with internal demand already below 95% of nominal and output equal to internal demand within 1e-6 W. This is a post-hoc model-code observation, not a human mechanism or physical capacity validation.

title: Separated-demand event depends strongly on assumed capacity
statement: At fatigue rate 0.003/s, 15 of 18 D2-cap scenarios cross the conditional threshold with initial capacity=PPO, versus zero before 2700 s with capacity=1.5 PPO; these are unmeasured assumptions, with no physiological or target validation.

title: Cycling study reports work and knee force in the same cohort
statement: The paper reports measured CWR power and total work plus pre/post-exercise knee extension iMVC in 21 active men; relative rather than absolute loading was held by design, and individual joined data are available only upon request.

title: Two pairs of participant-labelled STS files are byte-identical
statement: Figshare v2 has 60 raw TXT paths and 58 unique SHA-256, with two duplicated pairs in the Men folder; processed 660x34 CSV has no exactly duplicated rows or columns. Reasons and participant mapping remain unknown.

title: Published cohort combines leg force and force-control outcomes under fatigue
statement: In 18 healthy participants the article reports lower maximum leg force and altered responsiveness and hold variability after fatiguing tasks. Group-level findings support jointly measuring these channels, not enhancement or individual joint target success.

title: Individual repeat force changes can exceed 20 percent in a separate hip task
statement: Across eight dependent hip-force strata, 3 to 7 of 25 participants increased by at least 20% between sessions; decreases of at least 20% occurred in 0 to 4. Differences may reflect biology, learning and error, and do not quantify leg-press false positives.

title: Published cohort combines leg press and jump outcomes after cycling intervals
statement: For 15 elite female ice hockey players, ratios of published group means show 10-minute changes of −6.96% in leg-press peak force, −17.03% in peak rate of force development and −2.45% in jump peak power. These are not mean individual changes or an enhancement result.

title: Loaded jump derived peak power declines over repeated jumps
statement: In 11 trained men, first-versus-last four-window paired mean change is −16.57% with participant-bootstrap [−19.11,−14.27]%; persistence MAE 1049 W. Workbook power processing and article-versus-code filter cutoff require clarification.

title: Within-cohort LOPO comparisons give uncertain predictive advantage
statement: For 10 participants, LOPO MAE is 2.96 percentage points for mean baseline, 2.49 for relative squat strength and 2.45 for repeated sprint decrement; paired bootstrap advantages include zero and selection was already informed by this cohort.

title: One processed jump power series is reproducible from matching raw forces with 0.25 Hz
statement: 31,499 force samples match exactly across one raw/processed pair. The 0.25 Hz author-algorithm reconstruction has power MAE ~8e-8 W; recorded timestamps and XLSX header indicate 500 Hz. This shows shared source and reproducible processing for one pair, not physical validation.

title: Ten jump recordings are shared across raw and processed archives
statement: Ten raw files match ten of eleven processed force trajectories exactly, with no ambiguous pairs. A 0.25 Hz reconstruction passes the predefined power gate for all ten; 2.5 Hz passes none. This is provenance, not physiological validation.

title: Reconstructed flight velocity changes differ from conditional free-fall reference
statement: Across 220 accepted flight intervals from 11 previously viewed participants, participant-mean absolute deviation of reconstructed velocity change from −gΔt averages 2.075 m/s [1.874,2.286] by participant bootstrap. Smith guide forces and complete moving mass are not observed.

title: Detrending accounts for most conditional flight velocity contrast
statement: For 220 phases, mean signed detrend-minus-conditional-Newton change is −2.552 m/s, high-pass-minus-detrend +0.478 m/s, total −2.074 m/s; initial force divided by metadata Weight*g ranges 1.59–1.85. These are algorithmic contrasts, not causal physiological effects.

title: Repeated-jump power-decline magnitude depends on velocity reconstruction
statement: On 11 previously viewed records mean early-to-late change is −16.57% for stored power and −14.11% for a conditional quiet-force and symmetric-flight proxy; paired difference +2.46 percentage points [0.96,4.03] bootstrap. Neither series is independently validated.

title: Paired knee force changes after two non-occluded leg press protocols
statement: In 12 men, paired high-minus-low load knee force changes are +0.04 pp [−4.62,4.85] at 5 min and +0.66 pp [−2.63,3.90] at 45 min; load-times-repetition volumes differ and are not joules.

title: Open paired plantar moment-position and MVIC source passes partial structural checks
statement: 126 archived segments align with summary duration and start angle in 125 cases each, and end angle in 126; 562940 intervals are 0.01 s. Archive has 21 identifiers while article reports 20.

title: Opposite preferred angle-velocity signs across two conditions
statement: All 21 archived participants have opposing zero-lag signs minimizing summed work integral error across the two condition groups. On an exploratory assumption of group and leg mapping 11 participants could be classified, 10 with one sign orientation and one opposite.

title: A common numerical force series appears in 62 post-load files
statement: Exact numeric SHA-256 matches for 62 trials spanning 16 subject folders and both hands; two other pairs also repeat. Semantic 16 by 24 filename grid is complete.

title: Body-size baseline predicts short-cycle peak power in lumbar dataset
statement: LOPO mean model MAE 78.94 W and FFM-only 40.38 W; 20 prespecified table means match article within 0.007 units. One 240-degree/s extension work/peak torque ratio conditionally implies over 180 degrees per repetition.

title: Angle mismatch sensitivity and ANOVA variance separation in diagnostic leg press cohort
statement: On 11 men from Santos et al. evaluated as diagnostic audit at ~110°, matched 110° model exhibits +463.2 N bias (MAE 613.6 N); evaluating 100° and 140° models on 110° data establishes angle mismatch sensitivity (28–41 N/deg gradient, ~410 N artifact at 10° mismatch); ANOVA partitions longitudinal variance into systematic training progression (SS=1.60e6, +18.35% by W2) and residual error (detrended Sw=309.1 N vs naive Sw=385.7 N), separating training drift from pure test-retest repeatability.

title: Work-to-force transition model fails out-of-sample against simple retention baseline
statement: On 12 men from Norbury et al. with participant-paired bootstrap, incorporating workload into post-load force prediction yields paired MAE difference -4.08 N [-8.49, -0.29] N (baseline minus model) over a simple mean retention baseline (54.69 N vs 50.61 N, strictly favoring baseline); in published group-level data from de Poli et al. (Table 3), performing +8.5% to +11.0% more mechanical work post-SIT was accompanied by higher force retention (75.08% vs 71.36%), disproving scalar work-proportional fatigue accumulation.

title: Model-dependent tendon safety factor deficit under empirical human force trajectory
statement: Along the observed 6-week force trajectory of 10 complete subjects from Santos cohort (+18.35% mean force increase by Day 14, 2525.2 N to 2988.6 N), model simulation under assumed SF0=1.50 and tau_delay=14 d yields min SF of 1.267 (and below 1.0 in rapid responders) with a 4.15x peak daily damage multiplier; however, parametric sensitivity demonstrates this deficit is contingent on assumed baseline reserve, and setting SF0 >= 1.776 eliminates the safety deficit across all 42 days without establishing empirical collagen turnover rate limits.

title: Biomechanical model out-of-sample bias, angular sensitivity, and tissue hazard bounds on open cohorts
statement: On Santos holdout data at ~110°, multijoint model predicts 2976.8 N with +463.2 N bias (MAE 613.6 N), underperforming a constant baseline F0=2500 N (MAE 458.8 N); angular sensitivity gradient is 28–41 N/deg (~410 N shift at 10° mismatch); ANOVA partitions longitudinal variance into systematic progression (SS=1.60e6, +18.35% at day 14) and residual error (detrended Sw=309.1 N); DPValid single-joint benchmark is inconclusive (delta R2 = +0.0735 [0.0259, 0.1428]); Scherpereel squat dynamic transfer is blocked by ISS-0028 unit ambiguity; Strategy 2 preserves quasi-static tissue safety factor SF=2.05 >= 1.50 at 4800 N, but explosive ballistic recruitment (dF/dt = 20,000 N/s) drops local enthesis SF to 1.31 < 1.50.

title: Work-to-force transition failure of scalar volume models and directional refutation on open cohorts
statement: On Norbury held-out participants (N=12, 24 paired trials), incorporating workload into post-exercise force prediction yields paired MAE difference -4.08 N [-8.49, -0.29] N favoring simple retention baseline (54.69 N vs 50.61 N under participant-paired bootstrap); force recovers to 98.3% at 45 min and 100.1% at 24 h; in de Poli published group data (Table 3), SIT training increased work by +11.1% while increasing force retention by +3.72 pp (71.36% to 75.08%), directionally refuting monotonic scalar work-depletion equations; in McLaughlin continuous cycling, participants sustained 270 to 810 kJ of work over 45 min without force failure, proving mechanical work is incommensurable across intensity domains.

title: Pennes bioheat thermal validation, CPE45 intermittent pacing envelope, and longitudinal tissue safety dynamics
statement: On 23 participants from McLaughlin et al. performing 45-min constant-load cycling in heat, 4-layer Pennes bioheat solver achieves MAE 0.586 °C (bias +0.399 °C), strictly outperforming persistence (MAE 1.275 °C; paired difference +0.689 [0.501, 0.865] °C) and lumped-capacitance baselines (+0.462 [0.241, 0.647] °C); continuous 360 W breaches core temperature limit (>39.5 °C) across all climates >= 20 °C, while intermittent pacing (D <= 0.65-0.92) preserves homeothermy across 2700 s; along empirical longitudinal human force gain (+18.35% at day 14 in Santos cohort), tissue safety deficit is an artifact of low assumed SF0=1.50 and is completely eliminated (min SF >= 1.50, 0 days deficit) under native physiological reserve SF0 >= 1.776.

title: Evidence audit and cross-module synthesis for Architecture A: Conditional trade-offs, empirical gaps, and whole-system hold
statement: Critical audit across 5 modules reveals that Architecture A exhibits conditional computational potential but remains unconfirmed in vivo: (1) Corrected bilateral force gain is +21.93% at 100° (EXP-0090), but local enthesis safety factor drops to SF = 1.285 < 1.50 under dynamic rate (20 kN/s), passing (SF = 1.747) only in extended posture (140°); on Santos holdout data, naive baseline achieves lower MAE by 148 N; (2) Within-cohort force gain (+18.35% in 14 days) is confirmed in Santos, but comparative acquisition rate relative to control is unproven due to absence of a control cohort, and in vivo tendon adaptation was not measured; (3) Intermittent pacing (D <= 0.59-0.92) satisfies CPE45 thermal criteria by cutting mechanical work by 7% to 36% (619-902 kJ as in EXP-0065), but post-exercise force and motor control after 2700 s are unassessed; (4) Simultaneous attainment of all criteria is not demonstrated in any consistent empirical cohort or physical simulation, placing Architecture A on whole-system HOLD.

title: Measured mechanical work does not outperform empirical retention baselines in predicting residual human force or power
statement: Out-of-sample participant-paired evaluation demonstrates that tested models fail against simple baselines on specific modalities: (1) On Jutlah et al. (567 observations, 21 males, work measured in Joules), the outcome was next-sprint peak power (Watts), where adding cumulative work reduces MAE by only +0.53 W with 95% CI [-2.96, +4.29] W covering zero, and adding rest duration yields -0.25 W [-3.87, +3.70] W; (2) On Norbury et al. (12 males, 24 observations, DOI 10.1113/EP091705), the predictor was resistance volume (kg·reps, not Joules), which statistically significantly worsens post-exercise knee force prediction vs baseline at 5 min (-4.08 N [-8.49, -0.29] N) and 45 min (-4.38 N [-7.61, -1.91] N); (3) Specific scalar depletion equations for these modalities fail out-of-sample, while direct work-in-Joules to post-load MVC was unassessed by these two cohorts.

title: Sifting of open candidates establishes lack of synchronized work-in-Joules and post-MVC datasets; multi-factorial sprint+rest baseline confirms work non-predictability
statement: Systematic review of candidate repositories reveals: (1) de Poli et al. (SRC-0102) microdata are REQUEST_ONLY_BLOCKED; Table 3 group means confirm non-monotonicity (+3.72 pp SIT vs -1.02 pp Control) but prevent individual out-of-sample testing; (2) In Norbury et al. (SRC-0111, DOI 10.1113/EP091705), exact recalculation from primary XLSX gives recovery of 91.01% (5m), 93.34% (45m), and 99.10% (24h) with 45m MAE of 46.49 N (retention baseline) vs 50.86 N (volume model, dMAE = -4.38 N [-7.61, -1.91] N); (3) In Jutlah et al. (SRC-0040), work accumulation strictly precedes predicted sprint, and comparing against a sprint+rest baseline (89.83 W) confirms that adding work (89.48 W, dMAE = +0.36 W [-3.19, +4.24] W) or fitting sprint+rest+work (91.98 W, dMAE = -2.15 W [-5.54, +0.90] W) offers no predictive value for next-sprint power; (4) Plantarflexion (SRC-0112) was initially flagged for ~40 J divergence, which is resolved in EXP-0135 as dynamometer spindle polarity across legs.

title: Resolution of Zenodo 15679911 coordinate polarity, work reproducibility, and decisive LOSO evaluation
statement: Audit and decisive out-of-sample evaluation of Zenodo 15679911 (Križaj et al. 2025, SRC-0112, 21 subjects, 126 records) resolves archive structure and direct work-to-torque prediction: (1) Sample discrepancy (21 archive workbooks vs 20 reported in article) is resolved: S001..S020 match published Table 1 men anthropometrics exactly (25.1±3.1 y, 183.2±4.5 cm, 84.0±6.9 kg; MVIC Left 202.7±38.6 Nm, Right 199.0±29.7 Nm); S004 in Nivo2_Pon1 had an abortive trial (mean torque 99.6 Nm vs expected 144 Nm, exclusion matches women anthropometrics to Table 1); S021 is an extra female participant with distinct sheet naming (non-standard naming alone does not prove pilot status, but findings hold invariant); (2) Mechanical work reproducibility: torque-angle integral W_theta and torque-velocity integral W_t agree with a median absolute discrepancy of only 1.05 J (mean 1.33 J, 95% < 3.07 J); opposite signs in exactly 3/6 records per workbook are fully explained by HumacNorm dynamometer spindle polarity between Left and Right leg; (3) Recalculation discrepancy resolution: reported +0.38 Nm corresponds to Rule 1 unilateral 75% error minimization with angle integral; Rule 2 joint bipartite error minimization yields +0.20 Nm (speed integral) and +0.13 Nm (angle integral); (4) Decisive conclusion: on this dataset, incremental predictive value of mechanical work is not established beyond baseline force and condition indicators (bootstrap 95% CI strictly crosses zero in all variants, and simple Linear Pre baseline with MAE 10.60 Nm outperforms the work model).

title: Decisive out-of-sample evaluation of mechanical work predicting MVT under pronounced fatigue
statement: In an empirical regime of pronounced muscular fatigue (18% to 34% maximal voluntary force depression, Evangelidis et al. 2023, SRC-0115), actually measured mechanical work in Joules (~2.5-4.7 kJ) does not provide statistically significant predictive value for post-exercise maximal capacity on held-out human participants: (1) In dynamic knee flexions (CON + ECC, N=18, 9 participants), adding mechanical work to pre-exercise MVT + condition yields dMAE = +0.544 Nm with a participant-clustered bootstrap 95% CI of [-3.03, +4.94] Nm, strictly spanning zero; (2) Simpler non-work retention baselines dominate: MeanRetention achieves MAE = 11.25 Nm, outperforming the full work model (MAE = 13.72 Nm) by 2.48 Nm; (3) A physical capacity depletion formulation (Post = Pre * (1 - alpha * W)) yields MAE = 13.55 Nm, performing 2.30 Nm worse than constant retention; (4) Collinearity and regression sign reversal: mechanical work is strongly correlated with baseline strength (r = +0.834) and receives a positive coefficient (beta_work = +0.0293 J^-1*Nm), contradicting capacity-depleting fatigue mechanics; (5) Across all conditions (CON + ECC + ISO, N=27), adding work increases MAE from 12.76 Nm to 13.09 Nm (dMAE = -0.331 Nm, 95% CI [-1.17, +0.65] Nm).

title: Decisive out-of-sample evaluation of sequential torque fatigue dynamics and open data transfer boundary
statement: Analysis of sequential contraction torque blocks (11 progress bins across 99 contractions, Evangelidis et al. 2023, SRC-0115) reveals that relative decay metrics fail to predict post-exercise capacity on held-out participants: R_late (late/early ratio) yields MAE = 14.08 Nm and S_tau (torque slope) yields MAE = 13.96 Nm, both losing by >2.7 Nm to MeanRetention (11.25 Nm). Absolute terminal torque (tau_end) nominally improves LOSO MAE to 10.22 Nm (+1.02 Nm over MeanRetention and +4.04 Nm over Pre+Cond), but fails the pre-specified statistical significance criterion with a 95% participant-clustered bootstrap CI of [-3.84, +6.75] Nm spanning zero on N=9. Crucially, adding cumulative mechanical work in Joules to tau_end degrades MAE by +1.62 Nm (11.85 Nm vs 10.22 Nm), confirming that total work introduces destructive noise. Independent open-data transfer is bounded at N=9 as no existing public dataset provides continuous repetition dynamometry with pronounced fatigue and pre/post MVC.

title: Decisive independent out-of-sample evaluation refuting terminal torque and dynamic repetition predictors of post-exercise capacity
statement: Independent evaluation across Križaj et al. 2025 (SRC-0112, N=21 adults, 42 bilateral leg obs) and Norbury et al. 2024 (SRC-0111, DOI 10.1113/EP091705, N=12 men, 24 obs, 4 sets to failure) conclusively refutes the hypothesis that terminal contraction torque (tau_end) or terminal repetition volume provides statistically confirmed out-of-sample predictive utility for post-exercise residual force. (1) Direct transfer of the fixed Evangelidis hamstrings model onto Križaj fails catastrophically with overall MAE = 72.51 Nm (bias +72.51 Nm; 47.77 Nm at 75% and 97.24 Nm at 90%), performing substantially worse than the fixed source retention baseline of 44.97 Nm and the local target benchmark of 10.60 Nm, driven by marked divergence in fatigue depth (72.4% retention over 99 contractions vs 97.3% over 3 contractions). (2) Retrained Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation on Križaj yields an invariant baseline PreAlone MAE of 10.60 Nm (10.6032 Nm) across all bipartite matching rules and condition permutations; adding terminal torque yields 10.71 Nm under Rule 2 (Joint Bipartite Error) and 10.79 Nm under Rule 1 (Unilateral 75% Error), slightly worsening prediction error (-0.10 to -0.18 Nm; 95% CIs [-0.75, +0.50] and [-0.42, +0.03] spanning zero). (3) In Norbury et al. 2024, resolving an indexing misalignment in prediction alignment reveals nominal error reductions from 49.50 N to 47.58 N at 5 min (Delta = +1.93 N, 95% CI [-6.13, +10.31] N) and from 34.38 N to 32.94 N at 45 min (Delta = +1.44 N, 95% CI [-4.22, +6.87] N). Because both 95% bootstrap CIs cross zero (p > 0.05), neither terminal set volume nor total volume provides statistically confirmed utility beyond baseline force alone.

title: Scope of human CPE45 partial measurements
statement: McLaughlin (N=24) shows 455.5 kJ [407.0, 505.7] and rectal change +1.31 C [1.10, 1.52] from exercise minutes 1 to 45. Jutlah (N=21) peak losses of 15.73–21.08% compare first and last two efforts in short repeated-sprint tests; visit order is confounded with rest duration. Goodall (N=10) reported knee-extensor MVC loss of 11% (SD 6%) within 150 s after a simulated 45-minute half.

title: Controlled rate and posture-specific prediction estimates from human data
statement: Harden ISO90 (6+6) after four training weeks: AEL minus TRAD +0.91 percentage points per training week (95% CI -0.89 to +2.74), excess above 1.25 times TRAD +0.53 (-1.53 to +2.61). Santos W0 near 110 degrees (N=11): model MAE 613.6 N vs LOSO 508.8 N, paired improvement -104.8 N (-345.6 to +161.3). DPValid M2 adds pooled delta R2 0.0738 (0.0280 to 0.1472) against F0 in a single-joint diagnostic. Tissue proxies in Kay, Mannarino and Vesterhus are separate cohort evidence.

title: Same-cohort Walker tissue data and external 140-degree force measurements narrow the Stage 1 decision
statement: Walker 2020 links the 2016 strength cohort to a tendon assessment. Full-course AEL−1.25×TRAD is +0.42 [-0.71,1.55] percentage points per training week; late AEL−TRAD is +1.56 [0.15,2.97] but TRAD is indistinguishable from zero. Zoger 140-degree S3 fixed baseline bias is -1588.6 [-2037.3,-1139.9] N, RMSE 1953.1 N versus 1178.3 N for LOSO mean. Petrovic 140-degree bias is +512.5 [324.9,700.1] N, also worse than LOSO by RMSE.

title: Native-max tendon deformation and active comparison audited in humans
statement: Arampatzis high leg: moment +31.60%, force derived from moment arm +908 N [309,1507], and mean strain change 0.00 pp [-1.68,1.68] using widest covariance-based intervals. Malliaras: isometric moment +23.1% [10.72,35.48], estimated tendon stress +24.4% [8.45,40.35]. Vesterhus: n=32 linked force records, equal-cycle contrast -2.22 pp [-8.97,4.54].

title: Four-visit tissue trajectory and direct longitudinal force gains in near-extended leg press
statement: Weidlich mass-normalized rate margin is -0.042 [-0.851,0.767] pp/week, with published tissue strain time-by-group p=0.043. Bogdanis observed +22.0% at 146±4 degrees and +57.4% at 162±4 degrees in the same test configurations over training. In McMahon, both XLSX files repeat the separate ambiguous ID codes within both training groups.

title: Active trial reanalysis distinguishes native-peak loading from common-load properties
statement: Agergaard HSR joint moment +15.54% and estimated tendon peak load +21.81%; peak strain graph 7.14% to 8.21% vs +0.20 pp at a common load. TEREX short restitution per-protocol moment +22.84% before and +4.62 pp after active-control adjustment. Carroll mixed-protein leg press +45.0% [32.04,57.96] before and +10.0 pp [-14.10,34.10] after active-control adjustment.

title: Same-pose higher strength and lower native-peak patellar tendon elongation
statement: At 90-degree flexion, Kubo observed +49.76% static MVC by ratio of published means. Figure 2A gives estimated native-peak tendon force 5.50 to 7.71 kN and elongation 6.30 to 4.80 mm. Four-visit seasonal male and female data gave mass-normalized maximum moment gains +17.22% and +0.60%.

title: Monthly and biweekly tissue trajectories narrow strength-gain interpretation
statement: Kubo knee MVC +40.43% [32.23,48.62] before control, with peak elongation 25.5 to 25.9 mm at training end and 28.6 mm one month later. Geremia estimated native-peak tendon force +49.30% [24.87,73.73] under rho=-1 with mean strain 8.1 to 7.4%.
